# Why ʾAṯiratu is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **ʾAṯiratu** is what the evidence put back.

ʾAṯiratu rarely fights; she decides. Her scenes in the Ugaritic tablets show the queen mother at work — approached by the younger gods, saddling her donkey, speaking in the high god's tent, and settling what thunder cannot. In KTU 1. 4 the storm-god Baʿlu has defeated Yammu but has no house — and no standing — among the gods.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** ʾAṯiratu
- **ASCII form:** athiratu
- **Meaning:** "‘Lady of the Sea’ — the Ugaritic mother of the gods (rbt ʾaṯrt ym), consort of ʾIlu and intercessor for Baʿlu, KTU"
- **Domain of influence:** Lady of the Sea, Mother of the Gods
- **Pantheon:** Canaanite
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐎀𐎘𐎗𐎚
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 43 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**ʾAṯiratu** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *athiratu* and **ʾAṯiratu** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **ʾAṯiratu** lives at [/sites/athiratu/](/sites/athiratu/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/athiratu/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/athiratu/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/athiratu/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **ʾAṯiratu** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** — The Lady who walks on the Sea — the original maritime mother of the Canaanite coast.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The mother of the gods; the matriarch every Canaanite cult answered to.
- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — The mother of the gods; the divine family tree grows from her tent.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Canaanite tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Enūma Eliš](/texts/enuma-elish/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
